chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Amr ibn Ibrahim, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Ismail ibn Abi Qurra, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who borrowed one hundred dinars from a man and mortgaged his jewellery for one hundred dinars. Then the man came to him and said to him, 'Lend me the gold which I have mortgaged with you as a loan (for use).' So he lent it to him, and the security got destroyed with him. Is there anything upon him for the owner of the loan regarding that?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It (loss) is upon the owner of the security deposit which he had mortgaged, and he is the one who destroyed it, and there is nothing upon the wealth of this one (lender).'

key_terms.عَارِيَّةً: for use (loan of a non-consumable item)

ai.seo_question: Who bears the loss if a mortgaged item is lent out and destroyed?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that when a debtor lends out a pledged item, the loss of that item falls upon the debtor rather than the creditor, as the debtor is deemed the active cause of its destruction by granting possession. This ruling underscores the principle of *tawallud* (derivative liability) in Shia jurisprudence, where the owner retains responsibility for risks incurred through their own voluntary disposal of the asset, even if it is in the creditor's possession. The hadith highlights the distinction between mere custody and active usage in determining financial liability for loss.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from one of our companions, from Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen, from Amro Bin Ibrahim, from Khalaf Bin Hamma, from Ismail Bin Abu Qurra, from Abu Baseer,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who borrowed one hundred Dinars from a man and mortgaged his jewellery of one hundred Dinars. Then he goes over to the man so he says to him, ‘Lend me the gold which I have mortgaged with you as a loan’. So he lends it to him, and the security gets destroyed with him. Is there anything upon him for the owner of the loan regarding that?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It (loss) is upon the owner of the security deposit which he had mortgaged, and he is the one who destroyed it, and there is nothing upon the wealth of this one (lender)’.
en.sarwar: 17. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from certain persons of our people from Mansur ibn al-‘ Abbas from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from ‘Amr ibn Ibrahim from Khalaf ibn Hammad from ‘Isma’il ibn abu Qurrah from abu Basir who has said the following:

“About the case of a man, who borrows one hundred dinars and leaves as al-Rahn (security deposit) jewelries worth one hundred dinars, then comes to al-Rahn (security deposit) holder and asks him to lend him the gold which he has with him. Al-Rahn (security deposit) holder lends it to him and it is destroyed; if he owes anything to the man who has left al-Rahn (security deposit) with him. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is on the one who left al-Rahn (security deposit) because he is the one who destroyed it and al-Rahn (security deposit) holder does not owe anything, not even a grain.’”
